items.note: The page sets A(2^b)B(2^b)=C(2^b), bounds deg C and the coefficients, and spells out the reason the assignment says the paper leaves to the reader: reduction modulo x^S-1 'replaces each x^j by x^{j mod S}, so it leaves C unchanged exactly when deg C<S'. This matches paper lines 4183-4193 with T and S as in 4058 and 4145.

The page gives b=ceil(log2 n), q=ceil(n/b) nonnegative base-2^b digits, a correct worked example (181 = 5+6*8+2*8^2 with b=3, q=3), and the identity that the inputs are A(2^b), B(2^b), so the product is C(2^b) with C=AB.

Each link of the chain is justified: deg A, deg B <= q-1 gives 2q-2; 'Since q<n/b+1, we get 2q-2<2n/b'; T>=4n/b gives 2n/b<=T/2; T/2<S comes from the parameter choice (paper 4145). It concludes there is no wraparound because every exponent is below S.

The page shows c_j is a sum of at most q products of digits in [0,2^b-1], then uses (2^b-1)^2<2^{2b} together with q<=n (since b>=1) and n<=2^b (since b=ceil(log2 n)) to reach 2^{3b}, as in paper eq. (capacity).

errors.quote: Each $c_j=\sum_k a_k b_{j-k}$ is a sum of at most $q$ products of digits
errors.problem: Notation clash: the page uses b both for the digit width (b=ceil(log2 n)) and for the digits b_{j-k} of the second input B. The paper writes only the bound on c_j and does not reuse the symbol, so the formula as written is ambiguous. It does not affect the argument.
